items.title: Ray Ricker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 27, 2022
items.q: I had one guy that was so really good, really into Cannonball and was just Cannonball, Cannonball, Cannonball.

ctx.x: Yeah, I think it’s something you can’t force you know. And you know if everybody is more or less doing, practicing the same stuff that’s going to — I mean you get out what’s put in and if you all are more or less inputting the same stuff through you, you know, the same play-a-long records, you know, that’s how — well I mean it happens in America. I mean we can go into certain — we could be in Idaho someplace and go into a shopping mall and see the same stores there as we have here. So that’s happening that way…

I’m cracking up because if you look over my shoulder, I don’t know if you can tell but that’s Cannonball Adderley and he’s been my guy. And I saw him actually in Rochester a number of times. I mean it’s not the only person I listen to but for me he had everything I wanted from a saxophone player.
Yeah. Well there’s nothing wrong with that. Stan Getz was my guy you know.
